file_roles.evidence: 'Map<String, DesiredConfig> desiredConfigs = cluster.getDesiredConfigs();' is deleted from inside createHostAction and hoisted to the caller as 'clusterDesiredConfigs', now passed in as a parameter; findConfigurationTagsWithOverrides(cluster, host.getHostName()) is replaced by configHelper.getEffectiveDesiredTags(cluster, hostName, clusterDesiredConfigs). Recomputing the cluster's desired configs once per host is the wrong logic being corrected.

isStaleConfigs and calculateIsStaleConfigs gain overloads taking HostComponentDesiredStateEntity, so the entity is fetched once by the caller instead of each call doing 'sch.getDesiredStateEntity()'. The old single-argument forms now delegate, which shows the repeated per-call entity lookup was the problem.

The diff is two interface declarations only: 'boolean isRestartRequired(HostComponentDesiredStateEntity ...)' and 'HostComponentDesiredStateEntity getDesiredStateEntity()', plus the import they need. No behaviour lives here; it is the API adaptation the real change forces.

In convertToResponse, 'String publicHostName = getPublicHostName()' becomes 'hostEntity.getPublicHostName()' and 'getComponentAdminState()' becomes getComponentAdminStateFromDesiredStateEntity(hostComponentDesiredStateEntity), both reusing entities already loaded instead of re-fetching. getDesiredStateEntity() is 'hostComponentDesiredStateDAO.findById(desiredStateEntityId)', so each avoided call is a database round trip.

The diff only tunes the test cluster: innodb_buffer_pool_size=16G, key_buffer_size=16G, 'agent.threadpool.size.max=25' to 100, 'client.threadpool.size.max=25' to 65, and alerts.cache.enabled=true. The rubric counts configuration tightening as preventive; none of the defect lives here.

rationale: The report is a bare performance complaint with no stack trace and no log line, so the log location cannot be determined. The slowness surfaces in the same start/stop action-creation path that the fix optimises, which is why the relation is same-location rather than a separate producer site. Three of the five gold files remove repeated per-host database lookups; the interface file only declares the new methods, and the gce script only tunes the test cluster.
notes: contrib/utils/perf/deploy-gce-perf-cluster.py is perf test-harness tooling, not product code, and TEST_PATH did not filter it. Worth flagging as a benchmark defect: a localizer cannot reasonably be asked to rank a deploy script as a fix target.
